figures.title: Figure 1
figures.llm_description: Fig. 1 (a) Top and (b) side views of the Hf2MnC2O2 MXene monolayer. Spin charge density of the (c) FM and (d) AFM states of the MXene Hf2MnC2O2 monolayer. The blue and green colors represent spin-up and spin-down electrons, respectively. (e) Direct and (f) superexchange interactions. Spin-polarized band structures of (g) spin-up and (h) spin-down electrons.

figures.title: Figure 2
figures.llm_description: Fig. 2 (a) Top view of (a) Hf2MnC2O2 and (b) Sc2CO2 monolayers. Structural diagrams of (c) DW-(I) and (d) UP-(I) Hf2MnC2O2/Sc2CO2 het-erostructures. C, O, Sc, Mn and Hf are represented by gray, red, cyan, blue and purple balls, respectively. d, dO–O and dO–O are the interlayer distance, the minimum distance between the O atom in Hf2MnC2O2 and the O atom in Sc2CO2, and the minimum distance between the O atom in Hf2MnC2O2 and the Sc atom in Sc2CO2, respectively. The green arrow represents the dire

figures.title: Figure 3
figures.llm_description: Fig. 3 Evolution of the magnetic moments of Mn and C atoms as a function of the do–Sc: (a) Hf2MnC2O2/Sc2CO2-Pk and (b) Hf2MnC2O2/ Sc2CO2-Pm. (c) Change of the exchange parameter J1 with do–Sc for Hf2MnC2O2/Sc2CO2-Pk and Hf2MnC2O2/Sc2CO2-Pm. The equilibrium positions of Hf2MnC2O2/Sc2CO2-Pk and Hf2MnC2O2/Sc2CO2-Pm hetero-structures are marked with red and blue dashed vertical lines, respectively.

figures.title: Figure 4
figures.llm_description: Fig. 4 PDOS of Hf2MnC2O2/Sc2CO2-Pk at different do–Sc: (a) 2.71 Å, (b) 2.81 Å, and (c) 2.91 Å; PDOS of Hf2MnC2O2/Sc2CO2-Pm at various do–Sc: (d) 2.66 Å, (e) 2.76 Å and (f) 2.86 Å. The gray shadow highlights the enhanced orbital hybridization due to lager DOS.

figures.title: Figure 5
figures.llm_description: Fig. 5 Electronic band structures of (a) Hf2MnC2O2 and (b) Sc2CO2, (c) and (d) Hf2MnC2O2/Sc2CO2 Pk, and (e) and (f) Hf2MnC2O2/Sc2CO2 Pm. Green and red lines represent the contributions from the spin-up and spin-down channels of Hf2MnC2O2, and black lines denote the contributions from the Sc2CO2 monolayer.

figures.title: Figure 6
figures.llm_description: Fig. 6 (a) Band edges of spin-polarized Hf2MnC2O2 and ferroelectric Sc2CO2 with respect to vacuum energy Evac, as well as the schematic diagram of the charge transfer. (b) The average electrostatic potentials of Hf2MnC2O2 and Sc2CO2 along the xy-plane. Integrals of differential charge densities and the differential charge densities of (c, e) Hf2MnC2O2/ Sc2CO2-Pk and (d, f) Hf2MnC2O2/Sc2CO2-Pm. The green and purple colors represent charge depletion and accumulation, respectively.

figures.title: Figure 7
figures.llm_description: Fig. 7 (a) and (b) Device prototype of the Hf2MnC2O2/Sc2CO2 hetero-structure FET.

figures.title: Figure 8
figures.llm_description: Fig. 8 (a)–(d) Optimized geometries of the four structural states of P1, P2, P3 and P4. Electronic band structures of P1 (e) and (f), P2 (i) and (j), P3 (g) and (h) and P4 (k) and (l). Green and red lines represent the contributions from the spin-up and spin-down channels of Hf2MnC2O2, and black lines denote the contributions from the Sc2CO2 monolayer. The green arrow represents the direction of polarization.

figures.title: Figure 9
figures.llm_description: Fig. 9 Orbital-resolved magnetic anisotropy energy of Mn and Hf atoms for (a) and (d) the Hf2MnC2O2 monolayer and (b) and (e) Hf2MnC2O2/Sc2CO2-Pk and (c) and (f) Hf2MnC2O2/Sc2CO2-Pm heterostructures, respectively.
